Location: Colorado River Locks, near Matagorda (GIWW mile 441.5)
Item: UPDATE: Colorado River Lock daytime closures now reported through Nov 20
Details: A barge-line operations page updated Oct 27 now lists the daily closures for West Lock south sector-gate repairs as running Aug 19 through Nov 20, 8am–6pm, weekdays only (no weekends or holidays) – not ending Oct 23 as earlier notices said. Tows were waiting about a day on Oct 27. Why it matters: on Oct 24 this brief listed these closures as ending; they appear to have been extended four weeks, so a weekday daytime transit of the Texas GIWW at Matagorda may still mean a long wait.
Notes: What to do: call the Colorado River Locks lockmaster at (979) 482-7321 before you go; plan to lock through early morning, evenings or on a weekend. Uncertainty: the Nov 20 date comes from American Commercial Barge Line's page only – no Corps notice for the extension was found today. This corrects the Oct 24 'Route Open' row. Map point is approximate.

Location: Leland Bowman Lock, near Intracoastal City (GIWW mile 163, Vermilion Parish)
Item: UPDATE: Leland Bowman Lock back open after log jam – but queue limited, long waits
Details: The lock reopened after the Oct 20 closure when a log fouled the gate, but it is letting only a set number of boats into the queue, and tows were seeing delays of about 32 hours on the morning of Oct 27. Why it matters: the closure is over, but a recreational boat arriving at Leland Bowman should not count on a quick lockage – the west Louisiana GIWW is backed up.
When: Reopened after Oct 20 closure; ~32-hour tow delays as of Oct 27 2026
Notes: What to do: call the lockmaster before you get there – 337-893-4412, VHF 14 (as published in the Corps' February 2026 notice) – and ask whether pleasure craft can lock with a tow; carry fuel and water for a long wait. Uncertainty: reopening time and the queue limit come from a barge-line page, not a Corps notice. Map point is approximate.

Location: Florida's Atlantic coast & Biscayne Bay – Fernandina Beach to Ocean Reef
Item: Gale warning over for Florida's Atlantic coast
Details: The gale warning that ran from Oct 24 through 2am Wednesday Oct 28 has ended; no gale, storm or tropical warnings are up today for any Gulf or Florida coastal waters. Small craft advisories are still up in places into Thursday and Friday, and coastal flood warnings are posted along parts of the Florida coast. Why it matters: the worst is behind us and the coast is opening back up, but it's still a sporty window for small boats – and high water can cut your bridge clearance.
When: Gale warning ended 2am EDT Wed Oct 28 2026; small craft advisories into Thu–Fri
Notes: What to do: check your zone's marine forecast before heading out – small craft advisories run until as late as 8pm Friday in some zones. With coastal flooding, check tide height against bridge clearance boards. Ends the gale-warning rows from Oct 23–25. Map point is a representative mid-coast spot (Cape Canaveral).

Location: Calcasieu Lock, near Lake Charles (GIWW mile 238, Calcasieu Parish)
Item: Calcasieu Lock weekday daytime closures set to end Oct 30–31; more wall work in November
Details: The weekday 7am–7pm closures for north chamber wall replacement, in place since May 20, are scheduled to end Oct 30 (one barge line says Oct 31). Another barge line reports the lock reopened, with remaining guide-wall work suspended until November and expected to take 2–3 weeks once crews return. Why it matters: daytime weekday transits of the lock should get much easier from the end of this week, but expect a second, shorter round of work in November.
When: Daytime closures May 20 – Oct 30/31 2026; guide-wall work to resume in Nov (dates not set)
Notes: What to do: call the Calcasieu lockmaster before transiting – the Coast Guard's Oct 16 Local Notice lists (337) 477-1482 (seen in search results; the notice PDF itself wouldn't load today). Uncertainty: end date differs by a day between sources; a Coast Guard notice summary also mentioned further closures Oct 31 – Dec 18 that no other source confirms. Map point is approximate.

Location: POW/MIA Park, 5995 N US Hwy 1, Melbourne (Indian River, just north of Pineda Causeway) to Capt. Hiram's, Sebastian
Item: Hiram's Haul – 28th running of the 60-mile beach-cat race down the Indian River
Details: Beach catamarans and small multihulls from 14 to 22 feet (Hobie 16, F18, F16, Carbon 20) race 30 miles south down the Indian River on Saturday, party in costume at Capt. Hiram's Sand Bar on Halloween night, then race back Sunday. Why it matters: a fleet of fast beach cats charging down the Atlantic ICW on Halloween weekend – if you're cruising the Indian River between Melbourne and Sebastian, expect them, and if you're ashore, it's a fine show.
Notes: What to do: give the racing fleet room on the ICW Saturday and Sunday; to watch, try the Melbourne start or the finish at Capt. Hiram's. Organizer: Florida Catamaran Racing Series, 407-473-4180. The event page says the race goes 30 miles south 'to Captain Hirams' – the Sebastian location is ours, not stated on the page. Same weekend as FLIBS in Fort Lauderdale. Map point is the Melbourne start.

Location: Clearwater Community Sailing Center, 1001 Gulf Blvd, Clearwater (Sand Key, Clearwater Bay)
Item: U.S. Windsurfer National Championships in Clearwater
Details: The 2026 U.S. Windsurfer Nationals race right off the Clearwater Community Sailing Center in Clearwater Bay. Why it matters: a national championship you can watch from shore at a public sailing center – and a heads-up for anyone anchoring or transiting Clearwater Bay that weekend.
Notes: What to do: give the racecourse room in Clearwater Bay; for details call the sailing center at 727-517-7776. No daily race schedule or spectator details are published. Same weekend as the A-Class Cat Worlds warm-up across the bay at Davis Island YC and the AGLCA Fall Rendezvous at Orange Beach. Map point is approximate.

Location: Davis Island Yacht Club, 1315 Severn Ave, Tampa – around Egmont Key and back
Item: UPDATE: Egmont Key Race is Nov 21–22 – two courses, racing since 1935
Details: Now confirmed for Nov 21–22, with a 65-mile long course around Egmont Key and back to Davis Island and a 35-mile short course inside the Skyway Bridge for cruising and small spinnaker boats. The club calls it the oldest running sailboat race on Florida's west coast, started in 1935 as a warm-up for the Havana Race; the long-course winner takes the Houston Wall Trophy. Why it matters: the short course makes it a real option for cruising boats, not just racers.
Notes: What to do: Notice of Race posted Oct 19; register through Regatta Network or call DIYC at 813-251-1158. If you're transiting Tampa Bay that weekend, expect race traffic near the shipping channel and the Skyway. Earlier row (Oct 7) had only Nov 21 and unconfirmed courses.
